children: Novo Nordisk A/S (NVO, Financials) is out with fresh phase 3 results on its investigational CagriSema obesity medicine, which showed an average decrease of 25% of body weight after 68 weeks in overweight or obese women.
The analysis involved more than 2,300 women.

Strong findings were observed across menopausal categories in a second investigation with almost 1,900 women. 26.7% weight loss was seen in premenopausal women, 24.8% in perimenopausal women and 23.1% in postmenopausal women.
CagriSema combines cagrilintide, an amylin and calcitonin receptor analog, with semaglutide, the GLP-1 component in Wegovy.
The numbers important because it's less and less about the absolute weight reduction, and more and more about how much more weight loss newer combinations can provide.
CagriSema is one of Novo Nordisk's primary assets in fighting for market dominance as competitor Eli Lilly broadens its obesity portfolio.
The next thing to look at is how these results play out in regulatory filings and whether larger phase 3 data show the same level of effectiveness.

title: Novo's New Obesity Drug Just Hit 25% Weight Loss in Women
